summary.text: Emily Gallagher is the Democratic incumbent running unopposed for re-election in Assembly District 50, which covers Greenpoint and Williamsburg.
Before her election in 2020 she worked as a museum educator and public historian and was a longtime Greenpoint neighborhood activist.
According to her official biography, she led first-in-the-nation legislation in 2023 on building electrification and on corporate (LLC) transparency.

paragraphs.text: Gallagher was raised in the Rochester, New York area, according to her official Assembly biography; Ballotpedia, citing her 2020 Candidate Connection survey, lists her birthplace as Fairfax, Virginia.
She earned an undergraduate degree from Ithaca College in 2006 and moved to Brooklyn that year.

She worked in museum education and as an educator and public historian at the Tenement Museum and other local institutions, and in 2015 became Community Affairs Director for Hostelling International (HI USA), focused on sustainability and community engagement.

A longtime Greenpoint neighborhood activist, Gallagher co-chaired the group Neighbors Allied for Good Growth from 2008 to 2015 and began writing a weekly column for the local paper The Greenpoint Star in 2015.
In her 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she described herself as a member of Community Board 1 and a co-founder of the Greenpoint Sexual Assault Task Force.

She defeated incumbent Assembly Member Joseph Lentol in the June 2020 Democratic primary and won the November 2020 general election; her official biography says she was the first new member to represent the 50th Assembly District in nearly half a century.
She took office on January 1, 2021, won re-election in 2022 and 2024, and defeated Andrew Bodiford in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 85.5% of the vote.

Her official biography says that in the 2023 session she led two first-in-the-nation policies: the All-Electric Buildings Act, to phase out fossil gas hookups in new construction, and the LLC Transparency Act, on anonymous shell companies in New York.

According to the Assembly website, she chairs the Commission on Solid Waste Management and is a member of the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Correction, Election Law and Transportation committees, the Legislative Women's Caucus, the Task Force on New Americans and the Task Force on Women's Issues.
